text:
maria: Heads-up: seeing ~1.5GB extra GPU memory per-node on TP=8 after the allocator change (commit a1b2c3d). Reproducer: run ./scripts/repro_tp8.sh. Anyone seen similar?

kevin: yep saw it on dedicated perf runs. suspect fragmentation: allocator now splits large workspaces -> many small pinned allocations kept alive. cc @sasha

sasha: can you paste the nsys excerpt and which model/config? also which kernel selection policy was active?

maria: nsys snippet from run (TP=8, batch=1):
```
NSYS SUMMARY:
GPU0 used: 12134 MiB peak
NCCL bw allocs: ~240 MiB per-rank (send/recv)
TP shards: 8 -> kv-cache replicated per-shard ~128 MiB each
Temp fwd peak: 1.05 GiB (cuBLAS workspace spikes)
Total peak per GPU observed: ~13.7 GiB (expected 12.2 GiB)
commit: a1b2c3d (allocator: split large workspace into 16MB chunks)
```

oliver: hmm. that matches a hypothesis: we're creating an NCCL communicator per tensor-parallel shard and each communicator creates its own pinned comm buffers. With TP=8 that multiplies the buffer cost. Before we reused a single comm handle per model shard group.

jing: measured independently: comm buffers ~250MB * 2 * 8 = ~4GB raw, but overlap/ring reduces some -> net ~1.6-2GB extra. Also KV cache currently allocated as independent tensors per-shard on GPU instead of sharded views, so we replicate keys/values across shards in some codepaths.

ben: quick experiments:
- set REDWOOD_ALLOCATOR_PREALLOC_MB=2048 -> peak down ~600MB
- reuse-comm-bufs branch (maria/comm-reuse) -> peak down ~900MB but small latency +2% for batch=1
- switching to memory-efficient matmul kernels (cublasLt heuristics) -> another ~300MB saved but +5% latency on long sequences

sasha: plan: run three controlled experiments (1) reuse comm buffers across shards (2) allocate KV cache as views into a single preallocated slab (3) enable memory-saving kernel policy + measure latency/cost tradeoffs. We should also add NVTX ranges around NCCL calls to make the profiler output cleaner.

maria: opened PR #4821 for comm-buf reuse (bench results in PR). Patch reduces per-GPU peak by ~900MB on tp8/bs1. Latency regression small; will follow up with microbench for small-batch tail latency.

oliver: add a unit to loki/memprof that asserts no >10% increase in fragmentation after allocator change. Also add a diagnostic report that prints free-list histogram (chunk sizes) on OOM.

deploy-bot: perf-suite/tp8-mem-regen queued (will run on gpu-dedicated-28)

kevin: another knob that helps: REDWOOD_ALLOCATOR_MAX_CHUNK_MB=512 which forces big contiguous chunks and reduces fragmentation in practice. worth making that the default for Dedicated.

maria: agreed. next steps: merge comm-buf reuse, implement KVcache-as-views, add memprof tests, then evaluate kernel-policy impact. I'll post numbers from perf-suite when ready (tomorrow).
